newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products see gas oil slip on IPE.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products see gas oil slip on IPE.

text.p: Singapore oil products were steady to softer on Tuesday in a thinly discussed market with gas oil slipping on plunging IPE gas oil and crude futures, traders said.

The market saw few players, most of whom were away at an industry conference. A Singapore trader offered 150,000 barrels of gas oil at $27.60 a barrel for October 6-10 lifting fob. A US trader offered 200,000 barrels for end-September lifting at 20 cents over Singapore quotes fob, facing a bid at $27.20. Talking levels Tuesday were below the deal done Monday at $27.95 for end-September between a European major and a Swiss trader.

Traders said Indonesia recently bought 80,000 tonnes of gas oil from a trader for second-half October delivery at 75 cents per barrel over Singapore quotes c+f basis. Taiwan issued a tender to sell 0.3 percent sulphur gas oil for October 1-23 lifting which will close on September 17.
Two European majors offered jet fuel for end-September lifting--one for 150,000 barrels at $28.90 and another at $29.00, facing no bids.
The light end of the barrel was thinly talked with a Dutch trader offering 50,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline at $21.90 per barrel for end September/early October lifting.

October swaps were heard talked at $21.90/$22.20 but no trade was reported. Naptha remianed unchanged with little direction from either market talk nor crude. September swaps were unchanged from Monday's levels at $20.60/$20.70.

Traders were mixed on near term market direction for fuel oil. Some said India's recent tender to buy September cargoes would help boost prices. They said pockets of demand from China were seen with bids ranging at $112-$114 a tonne fob. Others said Taiwan's sale tender for 30,000 tonnes for Oct 1-10 lifting wwould depress prices. A trader was also currently loading a cargo from South Korea.--Singapore Newsroom (+65-8703084)
